what_happened: spiral_inherit silently rendered empty Ground truths + Hypotheses sections for an unknown number of boots. server.py:2670/2680 read g.get("insight")/h.get("insight") but chronicle entries store the body under "content" (memory.py:182, 358). Open threads section worked because it reads "question", which matches the schema. Write path was always intact — recall_insights returned full bodies for the same entries that rendered as "[domain] " with nothing after. Two-character-class fix in two places (commit bfacc42, sovereign-stack repo).
what_learned: When a renderer drops content but the data layer is intact, suspect a field-name mismatch between the serializer and the schema before suspecting the write path. The section that renders correctly tells you the serializer is plumbed in fine — the broken sections are reading a key that doesn't exist on those record types. Generalized: serializers that fall back to .get(key, "") on a missing field hide schema drift indefinitely. Prefer KeyError or required-field assertions in renderers ingesting typed records, or at minimum log when a fallback default is taken on a non-empty record. Inheritance was silently degrading for downstream instances long before the bug was visibly named — every instance that called spiral_inherit booted without ground_truths or hypotheses content, only domain tags.
applies_to: any serializer reading optional keys from typed records — boot rituals, lineage layer, prior_for_turn, anywhere chronicle entries are formatted into prose
